summary: William Wright worked in linguistics, studying at St Andrews, Halle-Wittenberg, and Leiden. He held posts at University College London, Trinity College Dublin, the British Museum (1861–1870), and was Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge (1870–1889).

Indologist Willibald Kirfel studied at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi, completing his PhD and habilitation. He worked as a librarian at Bonn University Library before becoming Bibliothekar, Privatdozent (1920), and ordentlicher Professor (1922) at Bonn.

Sinologist Wilt L. Idema earned degrees at Leiden under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé, also studying at Hokkaido and Kyoto. He served as Professor of Chinese Literature at Leiden (1976–1999) and Harvard University (2000–2013).
Win Than Tun works in history and archaeology, having studied at the National University of Singapore under Myo Myint.

Winfred P. Lehmann was an indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1937–1941). He later served as professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (~1986–2007).
Winfred Robert Martin was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College and as Librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

Wing-tsit Chan worked in philosophy and sinology, studying at Harvard (~1924–1929). He held positions at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1937–1942), Dartmouth College (~1942–1966), and Chatham University (~1966–1982).

Religious studies scholar Winnifred Fallers Sullivan studied at Cornell and Chicago (J.D., Ph.D.). She held faculty posts at Washington and Lee (1994–2000), Chicago (2000–2005), University at Buffalo (2006–2012), and Indiana University Bloomington (~2012).
Winston Kyan is a scholar in sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago, where he studied under Hung Wu and Linda Seidel.

Wm. Theodore de Bary worked in sinology, philosophy, and religious studies, earning degrees from Columbia and studying at Harvard. He served as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia (1953–2017) and president of the AAS (1969–1970).

Wolf Singer studied at the University of Munich (~1962–1968). He held posts at the Technical University of Munich, Goethe University Frankfurt, Ernst Strüngmann Institute, and the Max Planck Institute for Brain Research (~1981–2011).

Sinologist Wolfgang Franke studied at the University of Hamburg and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Peking University and Sichuan University before serving as the sinology chair at the University of Hamburg (~1950–1977).

Wolfgang Morgenroth, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Jena under Richard Hauschild and at Greifswald. He held academic posts at Jena, Greifswald, and Humboldt University of Berlin (Indology chair 1972–1994), alongside a guest professorship at Pune.

Wolfgang Schultz worked in philosophy and history/archaeology, receiving his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna. He was administrator at the Forschungsinstitut für Osten und Orient (1918–1921) and held the Chair of Philosophy at Munich (1934).

Sinologist Wolfram Eberhard studied in Berlin under Ferdinand Lessing. After teaching at several Chinese institutions, the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, and Ankara University (1937–1948), he was Professor of Sociology at UC Berkeley (1948–1976).
Woncheol Yun works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Stony Brook University and served as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University (attested 2012).
Woosung Huh works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and served as a philosophy professor at Kyung Hee University (attested 2012).
Wulstan Fletcher is an active scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Taklung Tsetrul Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (attested 1999).
Xi Cao works in computational fields and Tibetology, holding posts at Tibet University and Minzu University of China.

Indologist and linguist Xianlin Ji studied at Tsinghua and Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt and Emil Sieg. He held leadership posts at the Chinese Academy of Sciences and served as professor, vice president, and Life Professor at Peking University.
